reviews.text: Thanks Tiziano for the 5 stars even if unfortunately there was nothing else that could be done

I had to go a few weeks ago with my cat, who hadn't been feeling well that evening. There was only one doctor there, and after making me wait for almost half an hour, he practically shooed me away in a rude manner, saying he'd been with the current patient for at least an hour. I didn't even have time to explain what was wrong with my cat and therefore understand the urgency and seriousness of the situation.
I understand that the doctor was already busy with another animal, and I respect that, but the politeness and empathy were absolutely lacking. I won't be going back, neither in an emergency nor calmly.
Kind, professional, and always available to solve any problem. My Brus (French bulldog) is always happy to meet his doctors 🐶

I took my dog ​​for a check-up, they did 2 x-rays and assured me that nothing was found affecting the lungs, 6 days of anti-inflammatories as prescribed! After 6 days the dog was as it was when I brought him to them, we went to another doctor who put the dog on antibiotics for at least 10 days because the lungs are not clear and clean as claimed in this clinic!!! Translated into simple words: useless visit, a lot of money wasted and with high risk for the dog! Never again
Thanks for the 5 stars

Following two surgeries on my dog's foot pad for inflammation (approximately €600, and the problem was not resolved), I went this morning at 9:00 a.m., as communicated by the clinic, for a final check-up of the wound. After waiting for the appointments of the dogs present before us, we entered the office and the veterinarian present, finding no appointments on his calendar, informed us that he was unable to proceed, except to wait for all the appointments scheduled on his calendar to be completed, thus rejecting the appointment we had been given.
Obviously, I left the clinic without the scheduled check-up and will be looking at another clinic because:
- the office is completely disorganized due to the above,
- despite the expense incurred, the problem has not been resolved to date,
- the hostile attitude of the veterinarian present, who, to make us feel uncomfortable, even made us repeat our request out loud several times because he didn't understand the request.
The people present who had appointments were very kind, insisting that we get the appointment before them. But I could no longer tolerate this arrogance and presumption, without actually having resolved anything, and I decided to leave.
I will definitely never use this clinic again.
Thank you.
I always go there with my 4 year old cat for whatever it is and I feel very comfortable.

I've known the doctors who have been working there for 30 years.
I've brought dogs, cats, and rabbits to them!
The only thing missing is the fish!!
They're always available, competent, and friendly, but above all, they've solved every problem.
There's not much else to add, a true 24-hour veterinary reference point in the Eur Torrino area.
trained and available staff

An absolutely negative experience.
Hoping for a miracle, we brought our dog with very clear vital signs, no longer present; he was clearly comatose. The vet, after taking his temperature (he was severely hypothermic) and performing an X-ray, claimed he couldn't understand what was really wrong with the dog, even though he was fully aware that there was nothing more that could be done and what the fate of our poor dog was. He administered an IV (practically useless) and convinced us to leave him in the hospital, despite knowing that
our dog was now dying. He charged us €300 in advance and said goodbye. Two hours later, a colleague of his contacted us to inform us of the dog's death.
Not satisfied, he asked us for an additional €120 for the disposal of the body.
A degrading approach and professionalism for the veterinarian profession.
Professionalism and competence as well as politeness and kindness. Excellent!!

My furry friends have been treated since they were puppies. Five years ago, the team of Dr. Fabrizio, Dr. Giampiero, and Dr. Marino managed to diagnose my dog ​​Lola with Addison's disease. She was brought to them at the point of death. She is now eight and a half years old. Other vets hadn't figured out what she had... This morning, I took my other dog Holly to another vet clinic in the area because, ten days after she had a foxtail removed, she kept shaking her head (unfortunately, it was Saturday evening and mine was closed). There were two more foxtails. Thank you, Dr. Fabrizio and nurse Giulia.

I am deeply disappointed and saddened by my experience at the Eur Torrino Veterinary Clinic - European Veterinary Association, especially regarding the tragic loss of my beloved dog Wendy, a Labrador who did not receive adequate care.
Critical issues:
- Lack of empathy and sensitivity on the part of the Terlizzi veterinarian, who treated Wendy's case with unacceptable coldness and superficiality.
- Inadequate care and insufficient attention to my dog's needs, as confirmed by an independent medical report.
- Lack of clear and transparent communication regarding Wendy's health condition and available treatment options.
Actions taken:
I have reported the Terlizzi veterinarian's behavior to the Veterinary Association, providing all necessary documentation, including the medical report highlighting the deficiencies in the care provided. Furthermore, I have filed an appeal with the Justice of the Peace to obtain justice and compensation for the loss of Wendy.
I strongly advise against this clinic for anyone seeking professional veterinary care that is attentive to their pets' needs.

REPLY FROM W. MORRONE TO THE REPLICA from the Eur Torrino Veterinary Clinic - European Veterinary Association (owner)
one hour ago

I understand your response and your perspective on grieving, but the loss of Wendy is still a deeply painful experience for me, and the time it takes to grieve is, as you well know, very personal.
The Question of Liability
I fully agree that it will be up to the judge to determine any liability and whether the protocols were followed. My action has precisely this purpose: to shed full light on the facts. I would like to emphasize, as already specified, that a full three hours passed between Wendy's first and second cardiac arrests, during which we were inexplicably sent home with instructions to return the following day. Furthermore, I find it unacceptable that a veterinary emergency room is not equipped to perform an echocardiogram due to the lack of a sonographer, a gap that, in my opinion, severely compromised the chances of a timely diagnosis and intervention. I would like to point out that Wendy's health was excellent for an 11-year-old dog, an age that, even advanced, does not justify such a dramatic outcome, especially considering the lack of adequate diagnostic tools and the decisions made regarding her hospitalization.
The photos and the accusations of denigration
I have removed the photo of the dog in the morgue as requested. However, I would like to clarify that their publication was not motivated by bad taste, but by the intent to document the painful reality of that moment.
Finally, I assure you that my action is not harassment or media smear. I am simply exercising my right as a citizen to seek justice and clarity regarding what happened to Wendy. Reports to the competent authorities (ASL, NAS, etc.) are part of a legal process aimed at verifying the correctness of procedures and are in no way an attempt to defam an organization that, despite boasting a long history of operation, must nevertheless be held accountable for its actions. I am confident that justice will take its course and that the truth will emerge.

PLEASE read everything. It's very important that we, as customers, help each other.
Yesterday, June 15, 2025, I brought my Maltese because he wasn't feeling well. I found a highly knowledgeable, kind, and helpful doctor who examined the dog and administered the necessary treatment. He told me that if the dog continued to feel unwell, I should bring him back for hospitalization and further evaluation. During the night, blood tests were performed and further treatment was performed, which resulted in the dog's recovery. Today, we went to pick up the dog, as we were told, at 6:00 PM. We found another vet, not the same one from the night before. He treated us terribly, telling us that we only took the dog to the vet because we were tired of hearing him cry. When my dog ​​never cried, he was brought in because he had an emergency that occurred on a Sunday, so my usual vet was closed. The only clinic open was this one, because it says emergency room. We were told that since the dog isn't being treated there, I shouldn't have brought him. Now I wonder if I'm sick, I go to the emergency room, not my GP; the same goes for our animal friends. So what's this vet's moral code? Should I either send him to his regular vet, or should I let the dog die if I have an emergency when my vet is closed? I hope someone reads this review and protects themselves from this rude and self-serving person. Let it be clear: we paid every penny for our dog's well-being, and we would do it again a billion times over, but never again at this clinic if we have to be treated this way. I hope the doctor, reading this, will do some soul-searching and return to doing his job for the good of the animals, not his wallet!
I've been with them since their arrival...

I thank Drs. Mariotti, Terlizzi, and Tocca, who treated my cat Perla with great skill, professionalism, and empathy. The cat was cared for with great care during her hospital stay and also afterward for hemolytic anemia, which she was undergoing treatment for. I highly recommend this facility for your beloved furry friends.
